theater: 呼羅珊木魯夫至伊拉克札卜河

battle.name: 阿巴斯革命
battle.theater: 呼羅珊木魯夫至伊拉克札卜河
battle.brief: 公元746年起，阿拔斯派在呼羅珊木魯夫舉起黑旗，四年間由東向西席捲伊拉克，最終在札卜河擊潰末代哈里發馬萬二世。卡面羅馬弩砲早已不存於世，但它在攻城與壓制密集隊形上的任務，則由阿拔斯軍的配重投石機與弩砲交給一批從波斯、拜占庭學來的工匠完成。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 這是一場以改朝換代收尾的革命戰爭，交戰雙方的構成極不對稱。倭馬亞一方以末代哈里發阿卜杜勒·馬利克·伊本·馬萬（馬萬二世）為核心，帝國實際分成聯繫鬆散的三塊：敘利亞本部由哈里發本人與敘利亞軍隊坐鎮，伊拉克由總督優素福·伊本·歐麥爾·阿爾·費赫里控制，呼羅珊由總督納斯爾·伊本·賽亞爾控制。伊拉克與呼羅珊之間只靠驛道、糧船與文書相連，戰事一旦拉長，兩位總督便各自為政。倭馬亞軍隊的主體是敘利亞與伊拉克的阿拉伯部落騎兵、編入軍伍的波斯歸信者步兵，以及為數不多的拜占庭式工程兵；哈里發向拜占庭求援未果，卻仍從呼羅珊抽走精兵去補東線與西線，等於自己拆自己的牆角。阿拔斯一方則是一個跨族聯盟：骨幹是阿布·穆斯林在呼羅珊招募的波斯歸信者與阿布納出身的軍人組成的呼羅珊軍，騎兵比例極高；政治核心是哈希姆家系的阿拔斯兄弟，阿卜杜拉·伊本·穆罕默德（後來的曼蘇爾）與穆罕默德·伊本·阿里；再加上庫法的胡扎伊部族（蘇萊曼·伊本·哈里斯）、胡阿里吉派餘部、粟特與花剌子模的突厥系部落，以及後期倒過來的突厥部騎兵（齊亞德·伊本·薩利赫麾下）。兩造都沒有海軍，全部戰事在陸路與內河展開，這決定了後來每一場交戰的形狀。
countriesEn: This was a revolutionary war that ended in a change of dynasty, and the composition of the two sides was grotesquely mismatched. On the Umayyad side the core was the last caliph, Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, Marwan II, and the empire in practice fell into three loosely connected pieces: Syria proper, held by the caliph and the Syrian army; Iraq, controlled by the governor Yusuf ibn Umar al-Thaqafi; and Khurasan, controlled by the governor Nasr ibn Sayyar. Iraq and Khurasan were linked by nothing but post roads, grain fleets and paperwork, so as soon as the fighting dragged on, the two governors operated on their own. The Umayyad army was in the first instance Arab tribal cavalry from Syria and Iraq, Persian converts enrolled as infantry, and a small number of Byzantine-trained engineers. The caliph's appeal to Byzantium produced nothing, yet he still drew troops out of Khurasan to patch the eastern and western fronts, tearing down his own bulwark. The Abbasid side, by contrast, was a cross-ethnic coalition. Its backbone was the Khurasan army that Abu Muslim raised from the Persian converts and from the Abna, the sons of earlier converts, a force in which cavalry predominated. Its political core was the two Abbasid brothers of the Hashimite house, Abdullah ibn Muhammad, the future al-Mansur, and Muhammad ibn Ali, known as al-Jundaysabur. To these were added the Kufan Khuzza'i clan under Sulayman ibn al-Harith, the surviving Kharijites, the Turkic peoples of Sogdia and Khwarazm, and later the Turgesh horsemen who came over under Ziyad ibn Salih. Neither side had a navy; the entire war was fought on roads and rivers, and that fact shaped the form of every engagement that followed.
people: 阿布·穆斯林是這場革命真正的動力。他原是胡阿里吉派在呼羅珊的活動者與密使，奉命到東方建立網絡，後來依阿拔斯家的意思轉為舉兵，在木魯夫以夜襲拉起黑旗，數月之間聚起數萬人。他並非阿拔斯家的人，卻在四年裡握有全軍的實權，兩邊的關係自始緊張。哈希姆家的兩個兄弟站在後方：阿卜杜拉·伊本·穆罕默德（阿布·阿拔斯，即日後的曼蘇爾）負責在伊拉克的策劃與經營，穆罕默德·伊本·阿里（朱贊迪亞布爾）坐鎮呼羅珊；曼蘇爾有辯才、懂人心，軍功上卻遠不及這位將軍，兩人的矛盾最終以除掉阿布·穆斯林的命令收場。戰場上還有幾個關鍵人物：庫法出身的蘇萊曼·伊本·哈里斯·阿爾·胡扎伊，是阿拔斯軍在伊拉克最得力的將領，攻城與野戰皆出其手；格魯吉亞與亞美尼亞出身的王子赫拉克里亞斯（希拉格）改宗伊斯蘭後率驍騎為先鋒，札卜河一戰即由他打穿倭馬亞前鋒；齊亞德·伊本·薩利赫是阿拉伯將領，他麾下的突厥語系騎兵與突厥部可汗的部眾在關鍵時刻倒戈，改變了戰局。倭馬亞方面的核心則是兩位總督：呼羅珊的納斯爾·伊本·賽亞爾最早被木魯夫起義趕走，此後節節退讓；伊拉克的優素福·伊本·歐麥爾死守庫法與巴士拉，最終在駱駝之戰中被殺。哈里發馬萬二世在札卜河戰敗後西逃埃及，最終死於尼羅河畔。
peopleEn: Abu Muslim was the real engine of this revolution. He had been an organiser and emissary of the Kharijites in Khurasan, sent east to build a network, and he then turned to raising the banner on behalf of the Abbasid house, raising the black banner at Merv in a night attack and gathering tens of thousands of men within months. He was not of the Abbasid family, and for four years he held the real power of the army; the friction between the two was there from the beginning. The two brothers of the Hashimite house stood behind the front: Abdullah ibn Muhammad, Abu'l-Abbas, the future al-Mansur, handled planning and organisation in Iraq, while Muhammad ibn Ali, al-Jundaysabur, held Khurasan. Mansur had the eloquence and the political sense, but nowhere near the general's record, and the tension between them ended with the order to remove Abu Muslim. Several further figures mattered on the battlefield. Sulayman ibn al-Harith al-Khuza'i, a man of Kufa, was the most competent of the Abbasid commanders in Iraq, responsible both for the reduction of cities and for the open field. Heraclius, a prince of Georgian and Armenian origin who had converted to Islam, led the vanguard horsemen and broke the Umayyad advance guard at the Zab. Ziyad ibn Salih was an Arab commander whose Turkic horsemen, together with the Turgesh under their own qaghan, defected at the decisive moment and turned the battle. On the Umayyad side the core was the two governors: Nasr ibn Sayyar in Khurasan was driven out by the rising at Merv in the first place and thereafter gave ground step by step; Yusuf ibn Umar held Kufa and Basra in Iraq and was finally killed at the Battle of the Camel. The caliph Marwan II fled west to Egypt after his defeat at the Zab and died beside the Nile.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬弩砲是扭力蓄能的單發投射器，一發一具箭或一塊石，靠絞盤把力量存在扭曲的皮筋束裡，發射時一次釋放，專打城牆與密集隊形，羅馬人曾用它拆掉希臘人的城牆與城邦秩序。到了七四六年，這種武器早已在歐洲與近東消失數百年，戰場上沒有一台這樣的機器；它留下的位置，由伊斯蘭世界自己的攻城器械接手。功能最接近的是阿剌達，一種輕型、單人即可操作的投射機，發射大型箭矢對付城頭與人牆；再往上是曼加尼克配重投石機，以配重加速長臂，拋出石彈或繫在皮兜裡的碎石，用來砸塌牆根、掩體與城樓。兩者的技術譜系比羅馬弩砲更晚熟，卻在同一個問題上成熟：如何把投射力集中到一點。除攻城器械外，交戰雙方的個人裝備仍以弓為主：短身複合反曲弓配骨鏃，騎兵佩反曲弓、弧形彎刀與標槍，步兵用長矛、斧與圓盾；鎧甲是鎖子甲與鱗甲，頭盔為鐵質帶護鼻，盾牌有圓形木胎蒙皮的小盾，也有高身騎盾。馬匹是呼羅珊軍真正的戰略資源——中亞與呼羅珊的牧場供應了大量耐力型軍馬，使阿拔斯軍得以全騎兵作戰；駱駝負責搬運糧秣與攻城器材，長途穿越鹽鹼地與草原全靠牠們。倭馬亞方面的守城手段則是更老一代的辦法：拒馬、深壕與高牆，加上在水源上下手，據載優素福曾命人在庫法周邊的井中下毒，以拖慢對方的攻城工程。
kitsEn: The Roman scorpio on the card is a single-shot torsion engine: one heavy bolt or one stone, the power stored by a winch in twisted skeins of sinew and released in one stroke, aimed at walls and at densely packed formations. The Romans used it to pull down Greek walls, and with them the Greek system of city-states. By 746 the weapon had been gone from Europe and the Near East for several centuries, and not one machine of that kind stood on any battlefield in this war; the niche it had occupied was taken over by the siege engines of the Islamic world. The closest functional equivalent was the arrada, a light, one-man engine that threw large bolts at battlements and at walls of shields; above it stood the manjaniq, a counterweight trebuchet that accelerated a long arm with a counterweight and hurled stone shot, or stones held in a leather sling, to smash wall footings, barricades and towers. The technological pedigree of these machines is later than the scorpio's, but they matured on the same problem: concentrating the force of projection onto a single point. Outside the siege train, the personal equipment of both sides remained archery-centred. There were short composite recurved bows with bone or horn heads; the cavalry carried recurved bow, curved sword and javelin, the infantry long spear, axe and round shield. Armour was mail and scale, helmets were iron with nasal guards, and shields came both as small round wooden faces covered in hide and as tall cavalry turs. Horses were the true strategic resource of the Khurasan army: the pastures of Central Asia and Khurasan supplied large numbers of horses of endurance, and that is what allowed the Abbasids to fight as an all-cavalry army. Camels carried grain and siege matériel, and it was on their backs that the long crossing of salt flats and steppe was made. The Umayyads defended cities by older means, with spiked fences, deep ditches and high walls, and with the attack on the water supply: Yusuf ibn Umar is recorded as having ordered wells around Kufa to be poisoned, in order to slow the enemy works.
tactics: 革命的第一擊是木魯夫的夜襲，時機選在換禮拜的剎那，守軍的注意力被分開，黑旗升起之後守軍被驅散或隨軍官一同歸順，武器庫與糧秣被接管，木魯夫一舉成為阿拔斯派的據點。此後是全戰役最壯觀的一段機動：阿布·穆斯林不與伊拉克的倭馬亞軍正面糾纏，率軍自木魯夫出發，經尼沙普爾、雷伊與呼羅珊西境，穿越鹽鹼地與山道，行軍約兩千公里，在七四七年冬季逼近伊拉克。速行本身就是戰術，因為呼羅珊一旦鬆動，敘利亞的援軍就會沿幼發拉底河下來。圍城是第二段：阿拔斯軍自北面包圍庫法，倭馬亞總督優素福靠深壕、高牆與毒井硬撐，圍攻持續數月，最後因呼羅珊總督納斯爾·伊本·賽亞爾先一步西逃、兩地聯盟崩解而靠談判開城。真正的決戰是七五〇年十一月的札卜河之戰：阿拔斯軍以赫拉克里亞斯的先鋒騎兵為一翼，蘇萊曼·阿爾·胡扎伊統中軍，阿卜杜拉·伊本·阿里掌握全軍，靠騎兵的三面衝鋒與包抄；倭馬亞軍由馬萬二世與其子阿卜杜拉·伊本·馬萬在中央，兩翼是各部族兵與伊拉克兵。正面相撞之後，關鍵是突厥部的倒戈——大批突厥騎兵在交鋒中轉到阿拔斯一方，倭馬亞的中央陣形被從側背切開，軍心隨之崩潰。戰後的清理同樣是戰術的一部分：巴士拉在六月的駱駝之戰中被突破，優素福·伊本·歐麥爾戰死；馬萬二世西渡幼發拉底河入埃及，於尼羅河畔被當地勢力出賣，七五一年初被殺，倭馬亞朝在東方就此只餘一名逃亡的王子。
tacticsEn: The first blow of the revolution was a night attack on Merv, timed to the moment of the changing prayer, when the attention of the garrison was divided. Once the black banner was up, the garrison was scattered or went over along with its officers, the armoury and the stores were seized, and Merv became the Abbasid base in a single stroke. What followed was the most spectacular manoeuvre of the war. Abu Muslim did not entangle himself in a frontal struggle with the Umayyad army of Iraq; he marched out of Merv, through Nishapur, Rayy and the western reaches of Khurasan, across salt flats and mountain tracks, covering roughly two thousand kilometres, and came up on Iraq in the winter of 747. Speed was itself the tactic, because the moment Khurasan came loose, the reinforcements from Syria would come down the Euphrates. The siege was the second phase: the Abbasids invested Kufa from the north, the Umayyad governor Yusuf ibn Umar held out behind deep ditches, high walls and poisoned wells, and the siege ran for months until the flight of the Khurasan governor Nasr ibn Sayyar broke the alliance between the two provinces and the city was opened by negotiation. The real decision came at the Zab in November 750. The Abbasid line had Heraclius and his vanguard horsemen on one wing, Sulayman al-Khuza'i in the centre and Abdullah ibn Ali holding the whole army, and it worked by cavalry charge and encirclement on three sides; the Umayyad line had Marwan II and his son Abd Allah ibn Marwan in the centre, with tribal and Iraqi contingents on the wings. After the two fronts met, the decisive factor was the defection of the Turks: large numbers of Turkic horsemen crossed over to the Abbasid side during the battle, the Umayyad centre was cut from the flank and rear, and the morale of the army broke with it. The clearing up after the battle was tactical as well: Basra was carried in the Battle of the Camel in June and Yusuf ibn Umar was killed; Marwan II crossed the Euphrates west into Egypt, was betrayed by local powers beside the Nile, and was killed in the early months of 751, leaving the Umayyad house in the east with nothing but a fugitive prince.
data: 關於數字必須先說明：這場革命的數目主要出自九世紀的馬達里、巴拉杜胡里與十世紀的塔巴里等編年史，這些文本的兵員數字有明顯誇大，應當作量級而非統計來讀。可以核對的是時序與距離：密謀與徵募在七四六年前後展開，黑旗在七四七年六月於木魯夫升起（部分編年把起事記於七四六年），七四七年秋末大軍離開呼羅珊，越過近兩千公里的驛道與草原，七四八年六月進入庫法；七五〇年六月巴士拉的駱駝之戰，同年十月阿卜杜拉·伊本·穆罕默德在庫法被宣讀為哈里發；同年十一月十日札卜河之戰；七五一年初馬萬二世死於埃及。兵員方面，傳統記載稱阿布·穆斯林在木魯夫起兵時集得約三萬人，進入伊拉克時擴至十二萬；而札卜河一戰，編年史記阿拔斯軍三萬、倭馬亞軍十萬，這組數字明顯帶有以多勝寡的敘事目的，阿拔斯軍靠的並非人數，而是騎兵比例與聯盟的凝聚。傷亡沒有可信的統計，編年史通常只零星點名陣亡的將領。比較可核對的是地理與物資：木魯夫到庫法約兩千公里；札卜河戰場在庫法以東約二百五十至三百公里；敘利亞的援軍與糧船沿幼發拉底河與陸路南下，緩慢得多，馬萬二世在西奔時正是靠這條補給線才把追兵拖住。
dataEn: About the numbers one caveat has to come first: the principal figures for this revolution come from the ninth-century Madina, Baladhuri and tenth-century Tabari, and their troop numbers are plainly inflated, so they should be read as orders of magnitude rather than as statistics. What can be checked is the sequence and the distances. The conspiracy and the recruiting ran from around 746; the black banner went up at Merv in June 747, though some chronicles place the rising itself in 746; the army left Khurasan in the late autumn of 747 and crossed close to two thousand kilometres of post road and steppe, entering Kufa in June 748; the Battle of the Camel at Basra fell in June 750; in October of that year Abdullah ibn Muhammad was proclaimed caliph in Kufa; the Battle of the Zab came on 10 November 750; and Marwan II died in Egypt in the early months of 751. On numbers of men, the traditional accounts say that Abu Muslim gathered about thirty thousand at Merv when the rising began, and that the force was expanded to one hundred and twenty thousand before it entered Iraq; for the Battle of the Zab the chronicles give thirty thousand Abbasids against one hundred thousand Umayyads, a set of figures that plainly serves the narrative of the few overcoming the many, for the Abbasid strength lay not in numbers but in the share of cavalry and in the cohesion of the coalition. There is no credible casualty count; the chronicles usually name individual officers among the dead. More checkable are the geography and the logistics: about two thousand kilometres from Merv to Kufa; the field at the Zab lies roughly two hundred and fifty to three hundred kilometres east of Kufa; and the Syrian reinforcements and grain fleets came down by the Euphrates and the land roads, far more slowly, which is why Marwan II was able to keep the pursuit behind him as he fled west by that same line of supply.
cause: 三層原因疊在一起，才有七四六年的起事。第一是名分：倭馬亞出自烏邁亞氏族，並不在先知家系之列，呼羅珊的什葉派與一般信眾長期期待由哈希姆家系回歸哈里發之位；阿拔斯家正是先知叔祖阿拔斯·阿卜杜勒·穆塔利卜的後人，先知之裔當復位的說法在東行省已流傳數十年，阿拔斯兄弟所做的只是把它組織成軍隊。第二是阿布·穆斯的個人網絡：他原是胡阿里吉派派到呼羅珊的密使與煽動者，在總督納斯爾·伊本·賽亞爾猜忌下曾被囚禁，脫身之後把軍官、稅吏與不滿的波斯歸信者聯成一張網，給他提供了第一批骨幹。第三是呼羅珊本身的利害：呼羅珊是帝國最富的稅源與最大的兵源，歸信者與阿布納士兵為國家打仗，卻在軍利分配與官職升遷上排在阿拉伯部落之後；同時帝國把防守重心移往與突厥及交趾的邊境，徵召與調度常繞過呼羅珊總督，激怒了當地。第四是中央的虛弱：七四三至七四四年的繼位混戰耗盡了哈里發的權威，敘利亞、伊拉克與呼羅珊三地互相猜忌，誰都不肯為對方出頭；於是呼羅珊的問題變成敘利亞的問題，再變成一次更換王朝的戰爭。
causeEn: Three layers of cause came together to produce the rising of 746. The first was legitimacy. The Umayyads came from the Umayya clan, which is not among the families of the Prophet, and the Shi'i of Khurasan and ordinary believers had long expected the caliphate to return to the house of Hashim. The Abbasids were the descendants of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Prophet, and the doctrine that the family of the Prophet must reclaim the caliphate had been circulating in the eastern provinces for decades; all that the Abbasid brothers did was organise it into an army. The second was the personal network of Abu Muslim. He had been the Kharijites' emissary and agitator in Khurasan, had been imprisoned by the governor Nasr ibn Sayyar when the governor grew suspicious of him, and after his escape had woven officers, tax clerks and discontented Persian converts into a single web that supplied him with his first cadre. The third was the stake of Khurasan itself. Khurasan was the richest source of revenue and the largest source of soldiers in the empire; the converts and the Abna fought for the state, yet in the distribution of the spoils and in promotion they ranked behind the Arab tribes. At the same time the empire's defensive weight had shifted east towards the Turks and the frontier in Jiaozhi, and recruiting and dispatch repeatedly bypassed the governor of Khurasan, which enraged the province. The fourth was the weakness of the centre: the succession struggle of 743 and 744 exhausted the caliph's authority, Syria, Iraq and Khurasan grew suspicious of one another, and none of them would fight for the others. Khurasan's grievance therefore became Syria's problem, and then became a war to change the dynasty.
impact: 這場革命的直接結果是一個王朝的終結與另一個王朝的開端，但它改變的東西遠不止國號。倭馬亞朝留下的行政機器幾乎原封不動地落到阿拔斯朝手上：拜占庭與薩珊式的財政、驛站、迪萬與支付軍餉的文書制度都被保留下來，阿拔斯兄弟只用黑旗換掉白旗，就接管了一個能運轉的帝國，這說明這場起義是宮廷與軍隊層面的換血，而不是國家結構的重造。曼蘇爾後來把首都東移，於七六二年奠基巴格達，把波斯與中亞的商路以及伊朗的行政傳統接進哈里發的宮廷；阿拉伯語與波斯語、希臘語的經典在這個新都會裡被大量譯介，造紙術亦在此際西傳，成為之後數個世紀學術與行政變革的物質前提。族裔的次序同樣被改寫：歸信者與波斯官僚進入核心，巴馬基等家族把財政推向巔峰，又在下一個世紀把阿拔斯推向崩解。倭馬亞的絕種並非全族盡滅：敘利亞的一支逃往安達盧斯，於七五六年建立科爾多瓦的埃米拉特，藉真主唯一的哈里發這一名號與阿拔斯朝對立，成為西班牙倭馬亞王朝的源頭。軍隊的組成也從此改頭換面：突厥語系的盟部與奴兵取代阿拉伯部落兵成為阿拔斯軍的骨幹，邊防政策與內政重心一起東移。同一場革命留下的另一種記憶，是革命吞噬自己人的那種冷血：阿布·穆斯林在建國後兩三年內被殺，赫拉克里亞斯失勢後被弄瞎眼睛幽禁而死，阿卜杜拉·伊本·阿里同樣被致盲，這些都成了阿拔斯朝防範功臣的教科書案例。
impactEn: The immediate outcome of this revolution was the end of one dynasty and the beginning of another, but what it changed went far beyond the name on the banner. The administrative machine of the Umayyads passed almost untouched to the Abbasids: the Byzantine and Sasanian fiscal system, the post stations, the divan and the paperwork by which the troops were paid were all preserved, and the Abbasid brothers simply exchanged the white banner for the black one and took over an empire that already worked. That is the sign of a change of blood at the level of the court and the army rather than a remaking of the state's structure. Al-Mansur later moved the capital east and founded Baghdad in 762, splicing the trade routes of Persia and Central Asia and the administrative traditions of Iran into the caliphal court; Arabic, Persian and Greek learning was translated in quantity in that new metropolis, and papermaking reached the west at the same time, becoming the material precondition for the scholarly and administrative changes of the centuries that followed. The ethnic order was rewritten as well: converts and Persian administrators moved into the centre, families such as the Barmakids pushed the finances to their height and then, in the following century, pushed the Abbasids towards collapse. The extermination of the Umayyads was not quite the extinction of the house. One Syrian branch fled to al-Andalus and founded the emirate of Cordoba in 756, opposing the Abbasids in the name of the one and only God-given caliph and becoming the source of the Spanish Umayyad dynasty. The composition of the armies changed too: Turkic contingents and military slaves replaced the Arab tribal troops as the backbone of the Abbasid army, and both frontier policy and the internal centre of gravity moved east. The revolution left another kind of memory as well, the cold-blooded one of a revolution devouring its own: Abu Muslim was killed within two or three years of the victory, Heraclius was blinded and died in prison, Abdullah ibn Ali was blinded in his turn, and all of it became a textbook case of how the new dynasty policed its own benefactors.
result: 結果是倭馬亞帝國在東方的徹底崩潰。技術上的一條線：七四七年木魯夫黑旗升起，七四八年軍隊入庫法，七五〇年巴士拉的駱駝之戰中優素福·伊本·歐麥爾戰死，庫法解圍；同年十月，阿卜杜拉·伊本·穆罕默德在庫法的星期五講道中被宣讀為哈里發，白旗被黑旗取代；十一月十日的札卜河之戰決定了伊拉克與呼羅珊的歸屬，馬萬二世的中央陣被突厥騎兵切斷而崩潰，他帶殘部西走，於七五一年初在埃及被當地勢力圍攻，死於尼羅河畔的麥爾基里奧斯修道院附近，頭顱被送回伊拉克懸示，倭馬亞朝在東方的統治就此終結；其殘部在邊境又游鬥數年，直到七五七年才被最後清剿。政治上，另一條線同樣重要：革命的策動者阿布·穆斯林沒有得到他想要的東西，他在七五四或七五五年被曼蘇爾一方除掉，殺人的命令與執行的方式至今存疑；赫拉克里亞斯與阿卜杜拉·伊本·阿里先後失勢致盲；昔日的胡阿里吉派盟友被排除在新朝的職位之外，什葉派對馬赫迪的期待反而在民間延續，並在八世紀後半葉催生了伊斯梅伊利派。於是阿拔斯革命留下的，是一個新王朝對舊秩序的接管、對舊盟友的清算，以及一條把哈里發權推向中亞與波斯的全新地緣軸線。
resultEn: The result was the complete collapse of the Umayyad empire in the east. On the military line: the black banner went up at Merv in 747; the army entered Kufa in 748; in 750 Yusuf ibn Umar was killed at the Battle of the Camel at Basra and Kufa was relieved; in October of that year Abdullah ibn Muhammad was proclaimed caliph in the Friday sermon at Kufa and the white banner gave way to the black; the Battle of the Zab on 10 November settled the allegiance of Iraq and Khurasan, Marwan II's centre was cut apart by the Turkic cavalry and collapsed, and he marched west with the remnants, to be surrounded by local powers in Egypt and killed in the early months of 751 near the monastery of St Mercurius on the Nile, his head carried back to Iraq and hung up, and with that the Umayyad rule in the east ended; their remnants carried on in the frontier for some years more and were finally cleared out in 757. On the political line another fact is equally important: the man who had set the revolution going did not get what he wanted. Abu Muslim was removed by Mansur's side in 754 or 755, and both the order and the manner of his death remain disputed; Heraclius and Abdullah ibn Ali lost their positions and were blinded in turn; the old Kharijite allies of the movement were shut out of the offices of the new dynasty; and the Shi'i expectation of the Mahdi persisted in the countryside and, in the second half of the eighth century, gave birth to the Ismailis. What the Abbasid revolution left behind, then, was a new dynasty taking over an existing order, settling its accounts with its own allies, and a wholly new geopolitical axis that carried the caliphate's weight eastward into Central Asia and Persia.
